unavailable_fields.nccl_algorithm_protocol_channel_decision: Communication is off and distributed_backend is null on a single device; the capability field 'communication' is not_applicable with reason 'communication diagnostics disabled'; no NCCL collectives execute, so there are no algorithm/protocol/channel decisions to capture and nccl_tuning is inapplicable.
unavailable_fields.cross_rank_clock_aligned_intervals: ranks[0].status is not_applicable (disabled) and cross_rank.matched is empty; the clock policy forbids subtracting timestamps from different rank clocks, so no cross-rank interval can be formed.
unavailable_fields.per_collective_pcie_nvlink_bytes: The measured one-forward workload contains no collectives and no H2D transfer (input is GPU-resident and the model is preloaded before the measured boundary); PCIe/NVLink traffic is not invented from logical payload or memcpy sizes, and device_telemetry would only provide device-wide NVML rates with native windows, not per-collective bytes.
unavailable_fields.allreduce_reference_correctness_and_timi: No allreduce exists in this single-device inference workload, so collective_calibration's synthetic full-world SUM allreduce reference experiment has no matching operation to calibrate and is not a latency lower bound for this forward.
unavailable_fields.clean_host_dispatch_and_binding_costs: python_runtime is the only collector for host dispatch/binding costs, but it perturbs execution and its inclusive/self times are not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations; with no host-bound evidence in the trace this dimension stays unmeasured rather than approximated.
unavailable_fields.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_completion_bo: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only and GPU readiness/consumer completion may remain unknown even when run; it was not selected because the torch association is already complete and there are no gradient post-accumulate consumers under inference_mode.

rationale: Frozen objective: minimize latency_ms for one complete offline batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (single infer() call under torch.inference_mode) on one CUDA device, with images_per_second maximized and process-level peak_allocated_bytes minimized subject to a 0.95 throughput ratio; communication is off and distributed_backend is null. The torch collector already ran and coverage is complete (88/88 CUDA kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 root-only, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 backward/autograd ranges), so operator attribution - the primary latency evidence - is already in hand and no collector is rerun. nsys is available but not selected: no open overlap, CUDA-graph-tracing or attribution question remains that its timeline would resolve, since kernel associations and timestamps already exist in the torch trace. nccl_tuning and collective_calibration are inapplicable: one GPU, no collectives, no NCCL protocol decisions to capture and no allreduce to calibrate. device_telemetry is not selected: it samples device-wide NVML PCIe/utilization/memory with native windows, while the measured region has no H2D or collective traffic and the memory goal is the process-level PyTorch allocator peak, not whole-device memory. execution_timeline is not selected: its CPU-to-CUDA submit associations and per-device intervals duplicate the already-complete association, there are no gradient post-accumulate callbacks to observe under inference_mode, and it cannot bound GPU readiness or consumer completion anyway. python_runtime is not selected: it perturbs execution, its times are not clean scores, and no trace evidence indicates host dispatch or binding dominates the 88 substantial FP32 kernels of a single forward. candidate_diagnostics is deferred because no optimization candidate exists to diagnose at collection time. Requested fields are the objective metrics plus operator/kernel duration and allocator-peak breakdowns served by the existing torch trace; dimensions that cannot be observed are listed as unavailable with observed reasons rather than estimated.
